items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: So he taking my Uncle Clay to play the bass drum to give the youngsters ideas about a band being so big. So they brought me over and I would play the snare drum.

ctx.x: They were a lot cheaper then than them now.

Well I got the set and my Uncle Clay taking me to Old Man Chaloner for lessons. And Old Man Chaloner was a teacher. He didn't only teach you. He made you experience of learning to play instruments. He would have a big band of all of his scholars. On Monday you'd go to lessons. On Wednesday all his scholars would be in the band together.
